title: Not one of us (Mark 9:38–41)
hookLine: whoever is not against us is for us
last: LAST OF ALL, SERVANT OF ALL.

cards: The right jersey. The right school. The group chat you were or weren't added to.
Groups have unofficial rules about who's in. Now, just after the lesson about the child, John speaks up. Mark has told us Jesus nicknamed him and his brother the sons of thunder.
He seems pleased with his news. In the King James Bible: "Master, we saw one casting out devils in thy name, and he followeth not us: and we forbad him, because he followeth not us."
A stranger, doing good in the name of Jesus, and they shut him down. Listen to the reason, twice over. Not: he doesn't follow you.

teach.b: Jesus answers in three short words: "Forbid him not." Nobody who does a mighty work in my name, he says, can turn around the next moment and speak evil of me.

teach.h: NOT AGAINST US IS FOR US.
teach.b: Then the line: "For he that is not against us is on our part." The circle is wider than John drew it.

teach.h: A CUP OF WATER IS ENOUGH.
teach.b: And he sets the bar lower still: whoever gives you a cup of water to drink in my name, because you belong to Christ, will not lose their reward. A cup of water. The Hebrew Bible has a scene like this.
In the book of Numbers, two men named Eldad and Medad start prophesying in the camp without having been at the official gathering, and young Joshua begs Moses to stop them.

teach.h: MOSES: WOULD THAT ALL WERE PROPHETS.
teach.b: Moses says, in effect: I wish all the Lord's people were prophets.

teach.h: HE THAT IS NOT AGAINST US IS ON OUR PART.
teach.b: To be fair, the Gospels also keep a saying that sounds like the opposite. In Matthew, Jesus says whoever is not with me is against me. Christians keep both.

Some read Matthew's as about where a person stands toward Jesus himself, and today's as about how his followers treat people outside their own circle. Churches today differ, and argue about real things.
Some also set aside a yearly week to pray for Christian unity, side by side. The disciples asked who's with us. His answer was who's for us.

how: Some churches take part in a yearly Week of Prayer for Christian Unity, when Catholic, Orthodox and Protestant congregations pray together or visit one another.

games.q: you're John. you've seen a stranger healing people in Jesus's name, and you've told him to stop. how does Jesus react?
o: he thanks you for protecting the group.
he tells you not to stop him.
he goes to find the man himself.
games.why: "Forbid him not." the circle is wider than John drew it. even a cup of water, given in his name, counts.

practice: Think of someone outside your circle who does good: a person from a different church, or a different way of being Christian than the one you know best, the neighbor who runs the food drive, the nurse, the church down the road that worships in a way you don't.
Name one good thing they do, and mean it. If you pray, thank God for them by name; if you don't, just say thank you in your head.

wordCard.voice: John, the one who tried to stop a stranger casting out demons in Jesus's name. What Jesus answered: forbid him not.

carryVoice: Your line: not against us, for us. Even a cup of water counts. See you tomorrow.
